$comment: The roundness rule of the 3D models, language-agnostic. feature(scale) = paperFeatureMm * scale / 1000 metres. chordM(asset, scale) = min(largestM * max(scale, referenceScale) / (referenceScale * largestPerChord), chordPerFeature * feature(scale)): both terms grow in proportion to the denominator from 1:referenceScale on, so a solid sized by the scale keeps its segments and the chord never falls towards a coarser scale. A marker of `markerFeatures` features in diameter at a scale is a sphere of radius markerFeatures * feature(scale) / 2; three's SphereGeometry(r, n, ceil(n / 2)) has the triangles of the kernel's ellipsoid of n segments. Segments of a full circle of radius r: n = min(maxSegments[scale], max(minSegments, ceil(pi / acos(1 - chordM / r)), roundSegments when r > feature(scale))). Every solid of `kinds` is built about the Y axis with the radius r and the length 4 r: cylinder = revolve of the profile [[0, r], [4 r, r]], sphere = ellipsoid of radii [r, r, r], capsule = p0 [0, 0, 0], p1 [0, 4 r, 0], r0 = r1 = r, loft = two capped circular sections at [0, 0, 0] and [0, 4 r, 0].
